app_documentation:
The Hospital Appointment Booking System, branded in the design as 'CareBook', is a web and mobile-web application that lets patients find hospital doctors and book, reschedule, and cancel appointments online without double-booking. Its purpose is to replace phone-based scheduling with a fast, trustworthy self-service flow. Patients can complete a booking in four steps (search, pick doctor, pick slot, confirm), within the 5-step usability target. The system is built with React on the front end, a Node.js REST API with JWT authentication, an email/SMS gateway for notifications, and a PostgreSQL database.

The MVP covers five features. F1 Patient Registration and Authentication provides registration with email verification, login, and password reset, using bcrypt password hashing and role-based access control. F2 Doctor Search and Availability lets patients search by name, specialty, or department and view open time slots, while doctors set weekly availability that appears to patients within 1 minute. F3 Appointment Scheduling and Management supports booking, rescheduling, and cancelling. Slots are reserved transactionally, and a unique constraint on time slots plus a partial unique index on active appointments prevents double-booking. Online cancellation is allowed only at least 24 hours before the visit. F4 Notifications and Reminders sends email and SMS confirmations, 24-hour reminders, and doctor alerts for new or cancelled bookings within 5 minutes, with per-user channel preferences. F5 Admin Management Dashboard lets administrators manage doctors, departments, and schedules and run date-range reports showing total, completed, and cancelled appointments, with no-show and utilization insights.

The intended users are four roles: Patients, who book and manage their own visits; Doctors, who manage availability and receive booking alerts; Receptionists, who see appointments only and support bookings; and Administrators, who have full access to doctors, departments, schedules, and reports. The design uses a calm teal theme with Inter typography, card-based lists, a bottom tab bar (Doctors, Appointments, Alerts, Dashboard), and a mobile-first layout starting at 360px that scales to tablet and desktop. It meets WCAG AA accessibility standards.

Non-functional commitments govern support and operations. Pages load in under 2 seconds and bookings complete in under 3 seconds at 500 concurrent users. All traffic uses TLS 1.2+. Patient data is encrypted at rest with AES-256, and access to patient records is recorded in an audit trail. Monthly uptime is 99.9%, excluding scheduled maintenance announced 48 hours ahead. The delivery plan has 16 tasks (T1-T16) across DBA, Developer, and Designer roles, ending in end-to-end testing, double-booking race-condition tests, a 500-user load test, and a staging deployment. Key risks to monitor are concurrent double-booking, email/SMS gateway approval and delivery delays, performance tuning, privacy-compliance effort, and scope creep from receptionist features.

Design_v1 (teal design system, 6 screens: Sign In & Register, Find Doctors, Book Appointment, My Appointments, Notifications, Admin Dashboard; UI component library, responsive, accessibility, and animation guidelines)

Database_v1 (PostgreSQL schema with 17 tables: roles, users, user_roles, auth_tokens, patients, departments, specialties, doctors, doctor_specialties, doctor_availability_rules, time_slots, appointments, notification_preferences, notifications, audit_logs, plus documented design assumptions)

glossary.Time Slot: A concrete, bookable block of a doctor's time generated from availability rules, with status open, booked, or blocked; it is the unit that prevents double-booking via a unique doctor and start time constraint.
glossary.Double-Booking: Two patients reserving the same doctor slot; prevented by transactional slot locking, a unique (doctor_id, start_time) constraint on time slots, and a partial unique index on active appointments.
glossary.Availability Rule: A recurring weekly working window (day of week, start and end time, slot duration, effective dates) set by a doctor or admin and used by a background job to generate time slots.
glossary.RBAC (Role-Based Access Control): Security model enforced on every endpoint that restricts actions by user role: Patient, Doctor, Receptionist, or Administrator.
glossary.24-Hour Cancellation Rule: Policy that patients may cancel or reschedule online only at least 24 hours before the appointment; later changes require calling the hospital.
glossary.Audit Trail: An append-only log (audit_logs table) recording who viewed or changed patient records and other sensitive actions, supporting the privacy requirement for logged access.
